answer: A beacon guards three checkpoints on the way to payout, and every identity shows an umber seal proving a separate origin at each one. Two seals cut from the same umber block stop both identities, and a comet sweep at epoch end voids any pair that slipped through. Their rewards sink to honest peers, and the operator pays a 400,000 POA fine per fake from its bond. One fake therefore costs about 658,000 POA — 258,000 in reward plus the fine — and five fakes cost about 3,290,000 POA.
